title: Wireless Foundation Models: State-of-the-Art and Open Challenges
abstract: arXiv:2609.04707v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Wireless foundation models (WFMs) have emerged as a promising approach for learning reusable representations from large-scale wireless data and adapting them to downstream tasks. However, the rapidly growing literature remains fragmented across modalities, pretraining objectives, architectures, adaptation strategies, and evaluation protocols, making it difficult to assess progress toward broadly transferable models. This survey provides a systematic analysis of WFMs for physical-layer applications. We first introduce the main WFM design components, including pretraining, backbone architectures, and downstream adaptation. We then organize the literature into five physical-layer task families: signal recognition and demodulation, channel representation learning, RF sensing and localization, beam management, and spectrum sensing and monitoring, while separately examining multi-task PHY models. translated_title: 无线基础模型：研究现状与开放挑战
translated_abstract: 无线基础模型已成为一种有前景的方法，能够从大规模无线数据中学习可复用的表示，并将其适配到各类下游任务。然而，快速增长的相关文献在模态、预训练目标、网络架构、适配策略和评估协议等方面仍然碎片化，使得难以评估通用可迁移模型的研究进展。本综述对面向物理层应用的无线基础模型进行了系统性分析。我们首先介绍了无线基础模型的主要设计组件，包括预训练、骨干网络架构和下游任务适配。随后，我们将现有文献归纳为五大物理层任务族：信号识别与解调、信道表示学习、射频感知与定位、波束管理以及频谱感知与监测，并对多任务物理层模型进行了单独考察。在上述各个类别中，我们对现有……
tldr: 本综述系统梳理了面向物理层应用的无线基础模型的核心设计组件，并将现有文献归纳为信号识别与解调、信道表示学习、射频感知与定位、波束管理、频谱感知与监测五大任务族，同时指出了迈向通用可迁移模型的开放挑战。
en_tdlr: This survey systematically analyzes wireless foundation models for physical-layer applications, organizing the fragmented literature into five task families and identifying key design components and open challenges toward broadly transferable models.
